_about: Draft obligations for Rulebook in Motion, one per duty per addressee, drawn from the article texts in text/ as read on 2026-09-30. Each excerpt is copied verbatim from the quote of the paragraph the record names (a second or third excerpt, where present, comes from the paragraph its locator names). Every plain-language action is a draft awaiting Swann Ashworth’s approval, so every record keeps verify: true. Duties that fall on Member States, authorities, the Commission or ENISA are left out. NIS2 and CER duties reach entities through the national measures that transpose each Directive.

obligations.action: Take appropriate, proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage security risks to your network and information systems and prevent or minimise incidents’ impact.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage the risks posed to the security of network and information systems which those entities use for their operations or for the provision of their services, and to prevent or minimise the impact of incidents on recipients of their services and on other services.

obligations.action: Base your risk-management measures on an all-hazards approach and include at least those listed, such as incident handling, business continuity, supply chain security and cryptography.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: The measures referred to in paragraph 1 shall be based on an all-hazards approach that aims to protect network and information systems and the physical environment of those systems from incidents, and shall include at least the following:

obligations.trigger: finding that it does not comply with the measures in Article 21(2)
obligations.action: Take all necessary, appropriate and proportionate corrective measures without undue delay.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Member States shall ensure that an entity that finds that it does not comply with the measures provided for in paragraph 2 takes, without undue delay, all necessary, appropriate and proportionate corrective measures.

obligations.trigger: a significant incident
obligations.action: Notify the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority without undue delay of any incident with a significant impact on the provision of your services.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Each Member State shall ensure that essential and important entities notify, without undue delay, its CSIRT or, where applicable, its competent authority in accordance with paragraph 4 of any incident that has a significant impact on the provision of their services as referred to in paragraph 3 (significant incident).

obligations.trigger: a significant incident likely to adversely affect the provision of its services
obligations.action: Where appropriate, notify the recipients of your services without undue delay of significant incidents likely to adversely affect the provision of those services.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Where appropriate, entities concerned shall notify, without undue delay, the recipients of their services of significant incidents that are likely to adversely affect the provision of those services.

obligations.trigger: a significant cyber threat potentially affecting recipients of its services
obligations.action: Where applicable, tell service recipients potentially affected by a significant cyber threat, without undue delay, what measures they can take; where appropriate, describe the threat.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Where applicable, Member States shall ensure that essential and important entities communicate, without undue delay, to the recipients of their services that are potentially affected by a significant cyber threat any measures or remedies that those recipients are able to take in response to that threat.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Where appropriate, the entities shall also inform those recipients of the significant cyber threat itself.

obligations.trigger: becoming aware of a significant incident
obligations.action: Submit an early warning without undue delay and within 24 hours, indicating, where applicable, suspected unlawful or malicious acts or possible cross-border impact.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident, an early warning, which, where applicable, shall indicate whether the significant incident is suspected of being caused by unlawful or malicious acts or could have a cross-border impact

obligations.trigger: becoming aware of a significant incident
obligations.action: Submit an incident notification without undue delay and within 72 hours, with an initial assessment of severity and impact and, where available, indicators of compromise.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident, an incident notification, which, where applicable, shall update the information referred to in point (a) and indicate an initial assessment of the significant incident, including its severity and impact, as well as, where available, the indicators of compromise

obligations.trigger: a request from the CSIRT or the competent authority
obligations.action: Submit an intermediate report on relevant status updates when the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority requests one.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: upon the request of a CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority, an intermediate report on relevant status updates

obligations.trigger: submitting the incident notification
obligations.action: Within one month of the incident notification, submit a final report detailing the incident, likely threat or root cause, mitigation measures and any cross-border impact.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: a final report not later than one month after the submission of the incident notification under point (b), including the following:

obligations.trigger: an incident still ongoing when the final report is due
obligations.action: Where the incident is ongoing at the final report deadline, submit a progress report then and a final report within one month of handling it.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: in the event of an ongoing incident at the time of the submission of the final report referred to in point (d), Member States shall ensure that entities concerned provide a progress report at that time and a final report within one month of their handling of the incident.

obligations.trigger: becoming aware of a significant incident that has an impact on the provision of its trust services
obligations.action: Notify the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority without undue delay and within 24 hours, in place of the deadline in Article 23(4)(b).

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: By way of derogation from the first subparagraph, point (b), a trust service provider shall, with regard to significant incidents that have an impact on the provision of its trust services, notify the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority, without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident.

obligations.trigger: an incident that significantly disrupts, or has the potential to significantly disrupt, the provision of essential services
obligations.action: Notify the competent authority without undue delay of incidents that significantly disrupt, or could significantly disrupt, the provision of essential services.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2557 on the resilience of critical entities
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Member States shall ensure that critical entities notify the competent authority, without undue delay, of incidents that significantly disrupt or have the potential to significantly disrupt the provision of essential services.

obligations.trigger: becoming aware of an incident
obligations.action: Unless operationally unable to do so, submit an initial notification no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of an incident.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2557 on the resilience of critical entities
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Member States shall ensure that, unless operationally unable to do so, critical entities submit an initial notification no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of an incident

obligations.trigger: the initial notification of an incident
obligations.action: Where relevant, follow the initial notification with a detailed report no later than one month thereafter.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2557 on the resilience of critical entities
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Member States shall ensure that, unless operationally unable to do so, critical entities submit an initial notification no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of an incident, followed, where relevant, by a detailed report no later than one month thereafter.

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements
obligations.trigger: placing a product with digital elements on the market
obligations.action: Ensure the product has been designed, developed and produced in accordance with the essential cybersecurity requirements in Part I of Annex I.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: When placing a product with digital elements on the market, manufacturers shall ensure that it has been designed, developed and produced in accordance with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part I of Annex I.

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements
obligations.action: Assess the product’s cybersecurity risks and take the outcome into account from planning through maintenance, to minimise risks, prevent incidents and minimise their impact.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: manufacturers shall undertake an assessment of the cybersecurity risks associated with a product with digital elements and take the outcome of that assessment into account during the planning, design, development, production, delivery and maintenance phases of the product with digital elements with a view to minimising cybersecurity risks, preventing incidents and minimising their impact

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements
obligations.trigger: integrating components sourced from third parties
obligations.action: Exercise due diligence so integrated third-party components, including non-commercial free and open-source software, do not compromise the product’s cybersecurity.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: For the purpose of complying with paragraph 1, manufacturers shall exercise due diligence when integrating components sourced from third parties so that those components do not compromise the cybersecurity of the product with digital elements, including when integrating components of free and open-source software that have not been made available on the market in the course of a commercial activity.

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements
obligations.trigger: identifying a vulnerability in a component integrated in the product, including an open-source component
obligations.action: Report a vulnerability found in an integrated component to whoever manufactures or maintains it, and address and remediate it under Part II of Annex I.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Manufacturers shall, upon identifying a vulnerability in a component, including in an open source-component, which is integrated in the product with digital elements report the vulnerability to the person or entity manufacturing or maintaining the component, and address and remediate the vulnerability in accordance with the vulnerability handling requirements set out in Part II of Annex I.

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements
obligations.trigger: placing a product with digital elements on the market
obligations.action: Throughout the support period, ensure the product’s vulnerabilities, including in its components, are handled effectively and in line with Part II of Annex I.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Manufacturers shall ensure, when placing a product with digital elements on the market, and for the support period, that vulnerabilities of that product, including its components, are handled effectively and in accordance with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part II of Annex I.

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements
obligations.action: Determine a support period that reflects the product’s expected time in use: at least five years, or the expected use time if shorter.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Manufacturers shall determine the support period so that it reflects the length of time during which the product is expected to be in use, taking into account, in particular, reasonable user expectations, the nature of the product, including its intended purpose, as well as relevant Union law determining the lifetime of products with digital elements.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Without prejudice to the second subparagraph, the support period shall be at least five years. Where the product with digital elements is expected to be in use for less than five years, the support period shall correspond to the expected use time.

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements
obligations.trigger: placing a product with digital elements on the market
obligations.action: Before placing the product on the market, draw up the technical documentation referred to in Article 31.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Before placing a product with digital elements on the market, manufacturers shall draw up the technical documentation referred to in Article 31.

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements
obligations.trigger: knowing or having reason to believe, from placing on the market and for the support period, that the product or the manufacturer’s processes do not conform to the essential cybersecurity requirements in Annex I
obligations.action: Immediately take the corrective measures needed to bring the product or your processes into conformity, or withdraw or recall the product, as appropriate.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: manufacturers who know or have reason to believe that the product with digital elements or the processes put in place by the manufacturer are not in conformity with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Annex I shall immediately take the corrective measures necessary to bring that product with digital elements or the manufacturer’s processes into conformity

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: or to withdraw or recall the product, as appropriate.

obligations.action: Notify any actively exploited vulnerability in the product to the CSIRT designated as coordinator and ENISA simultaneously, through the single reporting platform.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union

obligations.trigger: becoming aware of an actively exploited vulnerability
obligations.action: Submit an early warning without undue delay and within 24 hours, naming, where applicable, the Member States where you know the product was made available.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements
obligations.trigger: a corrective or mitigating measure becoming available
obligations.action: Unless already provided, submit a final report within 14 days after a corrective or mitigating measure is available, covering the vulnerability, known exploiters and remedies.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements
obligations.trigger: becoming aware of a severe incident having an impact on the security of the product

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements
obligations.trigger: becoming aware of a severe incident having an impact on the security of the product
obligations.action: Submit an early warning without undue delay and within 24 hours, stating at least whether unlawful or malicious acts are suspected.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: an early warning notification of a severe incident having an impact on the security of the product with digital elements, without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of the manufacturer becoming aware of it, including at least whether the incident is suspected of being caused by unlawful or malicious acts

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements

obligations.action: Unless already provided, submit an incident notification without undue delay and within 72 hours, with an initial assessment and any corrective or mitigating measures taken.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: unless the relevant information has already been provided, an incident notification, without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of the manufacturer becoming aware of the incident, which shall provide general information, where available, about the nature of the incident, an initial assessment of the incident, as well as any corrective or mitigating measures taken

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements
obligations.trigger: submitting the incident notification
obligations.action: Unless already provided, submit a final report within one month of the incident notification, detailing the incident, likely threat or root cause, and mitigation measures.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: unless the relevant information has already been provided, a final report, within one month after the submission of the incident notification under point (b), including at least the following

obligations.addressee: manufacturers of products with digital elements
obligations.trigger: becoming aware of an actively exploited vulnerability or a severe incident having an impact on the security of the product
obligations.action: Inform impacted users, and where appropriate all users, of the vulnerability or incident and, where necessary, of mitigation and corrective measures they can deploy.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: the manufacturer shall inform the impacted users of the product with digital elements, and where appropriate all users, of that vulnerability or incident and, where necessary, of any risk mitigation and corrective measures that the users can deploy to mitigate the impact of that vulnerability or incident

obligations.action: Define, establish and implement an ICT-related incident management process to detect, manage and notify ICT-related incidents.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Financial entities shall define, establish and implement an ICT-related incident management process to detect, manage and notify ICT-related incidents.

obligations.action: Record all ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats; set procedures to monitor, handle and follow up incidents, identifying, documenting and addressing root causes.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Financial entities shall record all ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats. Financial entities shall establish appropriate procedures and processes to ensure a consistent and integrated monitoring, handling and follow-up of ICT-related incidents, to ensure that root causes are identified, documented and addressed in order to prevent the occurrence of such incidents.

obligations.action: Ensure the incident management process includes early warning indicators, classification procedures, assigned roles, communication and client notification plans, management reporting and response procedures.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: The ICT-related incident management process referred to in paragraph 1 shall:

obligations.action: Classify ICT-related incidents and determine their impact based on clients and counterparts affected, duration, geographical spread, data losses, criticality of services and economic impact.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Financial entities shall classify ICT-related incidents and shall determine their impact based on the following criteria:

obligations.action: Classify cyber threats as significant based on the criticality of services at risk, clients or counterparts targeted and the geographical spread of areas at risk.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Financial entities shall classify cyber threats as significant based on the criticality of the services at risk, including the financial entity’s transactions and operations, number and/or relevance of clients or financial counterparts targeted and the geographical spread of the areas at risk.

obligations.trigger: a major ICT-related incident
obligations.action: Report major ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority, through the initial notification and reports set out in Article 19(4).

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Financial entities shall report major ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority as referred to in Article 46 in accordance with paragraph 4 of this Article.

obligations.trigger: a significant cyber threat deemed relevant to the financial system, service users or clients
obligations.action: You may voluntarily notify significant cyber threats to the relevant competent authority when you deem them relevant to the financial system, service users or clients.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Financial entities may, on a voluntary basis, notify significant cyber threats to the relevant competent authority when they deem the threat to be of relevance to the financial system, service users or clients.

obligations.trigger: a major ICT-related incident that has an impact on the financial interests of clients
obligations.action: Without undue delay once aware, inform your clients about the major incident and the measures taken to mitigate its adverse effects.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Where a major ICT-related incident occurs and has an impact on the financial interests of clients, financial entities shall, without undue delay as soon as they become aware of it, inform their clients about the major ICT-related incident and about the measures that have been taken to mitigate the adverse effects of such incident.

obligations.trigger: a significant cyber threat
obligations.action: Where applicable, inform potentially affected clients of any appropriate protection measures they may consider taking.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: In the case of a significant cyber threat, financial entities shall, where applicable, inform their clients that are potentially affected of any appropriate protection measures which the latter may consider taking.

obligations.trigger: a major ICT-related incident
obligations.action: Submit an initial notification to the relevant competent authority within the time limits laid down under Article 20.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union

obligations.trigger: a significant change in the status or handling of the major ICT-related incident
obligations.action: Submit an intermediate report as soon as the incident’s status or handling changes significantly, then updated notifications as appropriate, including on the authority’s request.

obligations.action: Submit a final report once the root cause analysis is complete, whether or not mitigation is in place, and actual impact figures can replace estimates.

obligations.trigger: becoming aware of a personal data breach
obligations.action: Notify the competent supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours, unless a risk to people’s rights and freedoms is unlikely.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the personal data breach to the supervisory authority competent in accordance with Article 55, unless the personal data breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.

obligations.trigger: notifying the supervisory authority later than 72 hours after becoming aware of the breach
obligations.action: If you do not notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours, give reasons for the delay with the notification.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Where the notification to the supervisory authority is not made within 72 hours, it shall be accompanied by reasons for the delay.

obligations.trigger: becoming aware of a personal data breach
obligations.action: Notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: The processor shall notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach.

obligations.action: Document every personal data breach, covering the facts, its effects and the remedial action taken, so the supervisory authority can verify compliance with Article 33.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)

provenance.excerpt: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where that incident occurred.

obligations.addressee: providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market
obligations.trigger: establishing a causal link, or the reasonable likelihood of one, between the AI system and a serious incident
obligations.action: Report immediately once a causal link, or its reasonable likelihood, is established, and no later than 15 days after you or the deployer become aware.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: The report referred to in paragraph 1 shall be made immediately after the provider has established a causal link between the AI system and the serious incident or the reasonable likelihood of such a link, and, in any event, not later than 15 days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer, becomes aware of the serious incident.

obligations.addressee: providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market
obligations.trigger: a widespread infringement, or a serious incident that is a serious and irreversible disruption of the management or operation of critical infrastructure
obligations.action: For a widespread infringement or serious, irreversible disruption of critical infrastructure, report immediately and within two days of you or the deployer becoming aware.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Notwithstanding paragraph 2 of this Article, in the event of a widespread infringement or a serious incident as defined in Article 3, point (49)(b), the report referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall be provided immediately, and not later than two days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer becomes aware of that incident.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: a serious and irreversible disruption of the management or operation of critical infrastructure;

obligations.addressee: providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market
obligations.trigger: a serious incident involving the death of a person
obligations.action: Where a person dies, report immediately once you or the deployer establish or suspect a causal link, and within 10 days of becoming aware.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: the report shall be provided immediately after the provider or the deployer has established, or as soon as it suspects, a causal relationship between the high-risk AI system and the serious incident, but not later than 10 days after the date on which the provider or, where applicable, the deployer becomes aware of the serious incident.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: in the event of the death of a person

obligations.addressee: providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market
obligations.trigger: reporting a serious incident
obligations.action: Without delay, carry out the necessary investigations into the serious incident and the AI system, including a risk assessment and corrective action.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Following the reporting of a serious incident pursuant to paragraph 1, the provider shall, without delay, perform the necessary investigations in relation to the serious incident and the AI system concerned. This shall include a risk assessment of the incident, and corrective action.

obligations.addressee: providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market
obligations.trigger: investigating a reported serious incident
obligations.action: Cooperate with competent authorities and, where relevant, the notified body; inform the authorities before altering the AI system in ways that may affect cause evaluation.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: shall cooperate with the competent authorities, and where relevant with the notified body concerned, during the investigations referred to in the first subparagraph, and shall not perform any investigation which involves altering the AI system concerned in a way which may affect any subsequent evaluation of the causes of the incident, prior to informing the competent authorities of such action.
